title: Scientific Method and Lab Skills
description: Master the scientific method and essential laboratory skills.

lessons.title: The Scientific Method
lessons.content: Science follows a systematic process to test ideas.
examples: Observation → Question → Hypothesis → Experiment → Data → Conclusion
Hypothesis format: 'If [independent variable], then [dependent variable], because [reasoning]'
Control group: receives no treatment; used for comparison

lessons.title: Variables
lessons.content: Identify and control variables for a fair test.
examples: Independent variable: what you change
Dependent variable: what you measure
Controlled variables: everything else kept the same

title: Cells — Structure and Function
description: Study cell organelles and the differences between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
objectives: Identify cell organelles and their functions

lessons.title: Cell Organelles
lessons.content: Each organelle has a specific function, like organs in a body.
examples: Nucleus: control center (contains DNA)
Mitochondria: powerhouse (produces ATP via cellular respiration)
Chloroplast: site of photosynthesis (plant cells only)
Cell membrane: controls what enters/exits
Ribosome: makes proteins

lessons.title: Prokaryotes vs. Eukaryotes
lessons.content: Prokaryotes lack a nucleus; eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus.
examples: Prokaryotes: bacteria, archaea
Eukaryotes: animals, plants, fungi, protists
All organisms on Earth are one or the other

title: Photosynthesis and Cellular Respiration
description: Understand how plants produce food and how all cells release energy.
objectives: Write and explain the equation for photosynthesis
Explain how they are complementary processes

lessons.title: Photosynthesis
lessons.content: Plants use light energy to convert CO₂ and water into glucose and oxygen.
examples: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂
Takes place in chloroplasts
Glucose stores the energy from sunlight as chemical energy

lessons.title: Cellular Respiration
lessons.content: All living cells break down glucose to release usable energy (ATP).
examples: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + ATP
Aerobic (with O₂): most efficient — 36-38 ATP per glucose
Anaerobic: lactic acid fermentation in muscles; yeast produces CO₂ + alcohol

title: Atoms and Elements
description: Explore atomic structure, elements, and the periodic table.
objectives: Describe the structure of an atom
Use the periodic table to find element information
Understand atomic number and atomic mass

lessons.title: Atomic Structure
lessons.content: Atoms are made of protons, neutrons, and electrons.
examples: Protons: positive charge, in nucleus; number defines the element
Neutrons: no charge, in nucleus; affect atomic mass
Electrons: negative charge, orbit in shells

lessons.title: The Periodic Table
lessons.content: Elements are organized by atomic number in the periodic table.
examples: Rows (periods): elements with same number of electron shells
Columns (groups): elements with similar chemical properties
Metals, nonmetals, and metalloids have characteristic properties

title: Weather and Climate Science
description: Investigate atmospheric science, weather patterns, and climate.
objectives: Explain how the sun drives weather

lessons.title: Atmospheric Energy
lessons.content: The sun drives atmospheric circulation, which creates weather.
examples: Uneven heating: equator receives more solar energy than poles → wind and ocean currents
Convection cells: Hadley, Ferrel, and Polar cells move heat around the globe
Coriolis effect: Earth's rotation deflects winds to the right in northern hemisphere

lessons.title: Climate Factors
lessons.content: Multiple factors determine a region's climate.
examples: Latitude: closer to equator = warmer
Altitude: higher = colder (temp drops ~6.5°C per 1,000 m)
Ocean currents: Gulf Stream warms Europe
Rain shadow: leeward side of mountains is drier

title: Waves — Light and Sound
description: Understand wave properties and the behavior of light and sound.
objectives: Identify wave properties: wavelength, frequency, amplitude

lessons.title: Wave Properties
lessons.content: Waves transfer energy without transferring matter.
examples: Wavelength: distance between crests
Frequency: number of waves per second (Hertz)
Amplitude: height of wave (related to energy)
v = fλ (wave speed = frequency × wavelength)

lessons.title: Light and Sound
lessons.content: Sound needs a medium; light does not.
examples: Sound: longitudinal wave — travels through air, water, solids; ~343 m/s in air
Light: transverse electromagnetic wave — travels through vacuum at 3×10⁸ m/s
Electromagnetic spectrum: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, UV, X-ray, gamma ray

title: Heredity and Evolution
description: Connect genetics to evolution and natural selection.

lessons.title: Natural Selection
lessons.content: Traits that improve survival and reproduction become more common over time.
examples: Darwin's finches: different beak shapes evolved for different food sources
Antibiotic resistance: bacteria with resistance genes survive → reproduce → resistance spreads
4 requirements: variation, inheritance, differential survival, time

lessons.title: Evidence for Evolution
lessons.content: Multiple independent lines of evidence support evolution.
examples: Fossil record: shows change over time
Comparative anatomy: homologous structures (human arm, bat wing, whale flipper)
DNA evidence: humans share ~98.8% of DNA with chimpanzees
Biogeography: related species on nearby islands

title: Space Science — Solar System
description: Explore the solar system, its formation, and the planets within it.
objectives: Describe how the solar system formed

lessons.title: Solar System Formation
lessons.content: The solar system formed ~4.6 billion years ago from a spinning disk of gas and dust.
examples: Nebular hypothesis: cloud of gas collapsed under gravity → sun formed at center
Remaining material clumped together to form planets
Terrestrial planets (rocky): Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars — inner solar system
Gas giants: Jupiter, Saturn; Ice giants: Uranus, Neptune — outer solar system

lessons.title: Orbital Mechanics
lessons.content: Gravity keeps planets in orbit; Kepler's laws describe how.
examples: Planets closer to the sun move faster and have shorter years
Earth orbits the sun at ~29.8 km/s
Kepler's 3rd law: the farther from the sun, the longer the orbital period

title: Human Impact on Earth
description: Analyze how human activity affects Earth's systems and what can be done.
objectives: Explain the greenhouse effect and climate change

lessons.title: Climate Change Mechanisms
lessons.content: The greenhouse effect is natural; humans are intensifying it.
examples: CO₂, methane, and water vapor trap heat in atmosphere
Since 1880, global average temperature has risen ~1.1°C
Effects: more frequent extreme weather, glacier melt, sea level rise, ocean acidification

lessons.title: Biodiversity Loss
lessons.content: Current extinction rates are 100-1,000× background rates — a mass extinction.
examples: Habitat destruction is the #1 cause of species loss
Invasive species, pollution, overhunting, and climate change also contribute
1 million species are threatened with extinction (IPBES, 2019)

title: Engineering Design Process
description: Apply the engineering design process to solve a real-world problem.
objectives: Define a problem and establish criteria and constraints

lessons.title: The EDP
lessons.content: Engineers follow an iterative design process.
examples: Define: What is the problem? What are the criteria (what it must do) and constraints (limits)?
Brainstorm: Generate many possible solutions
Prototype: Build a testable model
Test: Evaluate against criteria
Improve: Use test results to refine the design
